verdict.rationale: Google Authenticator does offer a QR-code based transfer/export mechanism (docs-3, docs-11, comm-9, comm-18), but this produces a proprietary encoded QR payload meant for re-import into another Authenticator instance, not an open, human-readable secret export. Community evidence directly contradicts the 'open format, no lock-in' claim: users report Google 'makes it stupendously difficult to just get a simple text export to a file' and that the app 'does not allow you to include your codes in your backup, even when it's encrypted' (comm-6, comm-17), with several noting reliance on Google account survival for portability (comm-7, comm-12). Missing for 10: documented plain-text/CSV export, open standard export format, and independent confirmation that secrets can be freely moved to arbitrary third-party apps without QR/proprietary encoding.
